items.title: Reported adverse event with the TriClip device for tricuspid Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: Analysis of the MAUDE database.
items.abstract: The TriClip system (Abbott Cardiovascular) received United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval on April 2, 2024, becoming the first dedicated device for tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER). Pivotal trial data demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in quality of life with a favorable safety profile. However, real-world adverse events data following broad clinical adoption remain limited. We queried the FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database to characterize adverse events reported during the first year following FDA approval of the TriClip system (April 2, 2024-April 1, 2025). A total of 723 adverse event reports from 634 patients were identified. Single leaflet device attachment (SLDA) was the most frequently reported adverse event (n = 313, 43.3%). SLDA was identified intra-procedurally in 136 cases (43.5%). The majority of SLDA events were managed with additional clip implantation (n = 195, 62.3%), while surgical management was uncommon (n = 7, 2.2%). Device malfunction was the second most frequent adverse event (n = 221, 30.6%), followed by leaflet injury (n = 96, 13.3%). Device embolization was infrequently reported (n = 10, 1.4%), with half successfully retrieved percutaneously. All-cause death was reported in four cases. The number of reported events increased from 326 in the first 6 months to 391 in the subsequent 6 months, consistent with growing clinical adoption, while SLDA remained the most common event across both intervals. In the first year following FDA approval of TriClip, SLDA was the most common reported event and was predominantly managed with additional clip implantation, with surgical intervention rarely required. Because the MAUDE database lacks a procedural denominator, reports reflect the distribution of adverse event types rather than the true incidence rate.

items.title: Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane Block Improves Perioperative Analgesia in Transfemoral Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: To evaluate, as the primary efficacy endpoint, the difference in perioperative numeric rating scale (NRS) pain scores between patients receiving a transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block and those receiving a sham block during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Randomized, sham-controlled, prospective clinical trial with blinding of participants, procedural operators, outcome assessors, and statistician. Cardiac intervention laboratory of a tertiary hospital of an institute of cardiology. 18 years or older and presenting with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and an indication for transfemoral TAVI. Ultrasound-guided TAP block versus sham block. Numeric rating scale scores were significantly higher in the sham-control group (SCG) than in the TAP block group (TAPG) at the T3 (2.17 ± 0.41 v 0.54 ± 0.40; p = 0.006) and T4 time points (4.00 ± 0.50 v 2.00 ± 0.49; p = 0.007). Total intraprocedural fentanyl consumption was reduced in the TAPG compared with the SCG (median 75 v 100 µg; p = 0.010). A greater number of patients in the SCG required rescue sedoanalgesia compared with the TAPG (73.9% v 4.2%; p < 0.001). Intraoperative unexpected patient movement scores were lower in the TAPG than the SCG (p < 0.001). Monitored anesthesia care combined with TAP block improves the analgesic profile and procedural stability in patients undergoing TAVI.

Prognostic Stratification Value of Baseline Serum Amyloid A in Advanced Gastric Cancer Patients Receiving PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibitors.
items.abstract: Serum amyloid A (SAA), an acute-phase protein reflecting systemic inflammatory status, may provide prognostic information in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving immunotherapy. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic stratification value of baseline SAA in patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. We retrospectively analyzed 87 patients with advanced gastric cancer who received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy at Zhejiang Cancer Hospital between June 2019 and July 2023. Baseline SAA, C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin (ALB), and clinical characteristics were collected at treatment initiation. Optimal cut-off values were determined using X-tile analysis. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression models. The optimal cut-off value for baseline SAA was 13 mg/L. Compared with patients with SAA > 13 mg/L, those with SAA ≤ 13 mg/L had significantly longer overall survival (OS) (15.8 vs. 10.8 months, p = 0.004) and a lower risk of death (HR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.33-0.81). Progression-free survival (PFS) was also improved in the SAA ≤ 13 mg/L group (HR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.33-0.85; log-rank p = 0.007). No significant difference was observed in Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1-based treatment response between groups. Patients with SAA > 13 mg/L showed higher CRP levels and lower ALB levels (both p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, peritoneal metastasis and prior radical gastrectomy remained independently associated with OS, whereas SAA lost statistical significance after adjustment. Elevated baseline SAA was associated with poorer OS and PFS in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. SAA may reflect systemic inflammatory-host status and serve as an accessible biomarker for prognostic risk stratification, although prospective validation is required.

Exosome-inspired biomimetic nanocarriers: Biological principles, fabrication strategies, characterization, and therapeutic applications.
items.abstract: Biomimetic nanocarriers inspired by exosomes have emerged as a transformative strategy for precision drug delivery by combining the biological advantages of naturally derived extracellular vesicles with the scalability and tunability of synthetic nanotechnology. Native exosomes exhibit intrinsic immune evasion, membrane stability, ligand-mediated cellular tropism, and the ability to traverse complex biological barrier properties that conventional nanocarriers have struggled to replicate. This review systematically discusses the biological basis of exosomes, including their biogenesis, molecular composition, and intercellular communication roles, and translates these principles into engineering strategies for designing exosome-inspired biomimetic nanocarriers. We critically examine major biomimetic platforms such as cell membrane-coated nanoparticles, hybrid exosome-synthetic vesicles, lipid-based exosome mimetics, and polymeric biomimetic assemblies, with emphasis on fabrication techniques, drug loading approaches, targeting mechanisms, and advanced characterization methods. Recent therapeutic applications across oncology, central nervous system disorders, immunotherapy, gene and RNA delivery, and regenerative medicine are summarised with comparative insights into mechanistic performance. Furthermore, key challenges related to safety, manufacturing scalability, regulatory considerations, and quality control are discussed. Emerging trends, including microfluidic manufacturing, quality-by-design frameworks, and artificial intelligence-assisted nanocarrier optimization, are highlighted as future directions. Finally, we outline critical research gaps and propose a translational roadmap for clinical development of exosome-inspired biomimetic nanocarriers.

items.title: Liver transplantation for portal vein tumor thrombus in the immunotherapy era: outcomes and risk stratification in a multicentric study.
items.abstract: Immune-checkpoint-inhibitors (ICIs) role in liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) remains undefined. This study defines outcomes and selection criteria in patients with PVTT. Seventy patients with HCC and PVTT across 14 international centers were analyzed. Three cohorts were studied: ICI+LT (n=24), LT without ICI (n=31), and ICI without LT (n=15). Cox regression analysis identified predictors of survival and defined a high-risk subgroup. Compared with LT-alone patients, ICI+LT achieved higher radiographic response rates (95.8%vs54.8%, p=0.01), longer downstaging time (6vs2.5 months, p=0.028), smaller tumor diameter (1.5vs2.3 cm, p=0.01) and lower Vp3-Vp4 burden (4.2%vs25.8%, p=0.04) at LT. Independent predictors of improved OS were complete radiographic response (HR 0.27, p<0.001), AFP reduction ≥50% (HR 0.48, p=0.01), and meeting Milan criteria (HR 0.35, p<0.001). Vp3-4 (HR 6.00, p=0.008) predicted worse survival. In an exploratory, high-risk subgroup, (no radiographic response, AFP reduction ≤50%, no downstaging, and PVTT at LT), ICI+LT was associated with improved survival compared with LT alone (3-year OS 80.0%vs54.9%, p=0.048; 3-year RFS 68.6%vs41.6%, p=0.023). Well-selected, high-risk patients with PVTT achieved encouraging post-transplant survival. ICI-based therapy may improve oncologic outcomes, highlighting tumor biology's role in patient selection and immunotherapy use in transplant pathways.

items.title: Optimization of Lentiviral Transduction in NK92 Cells: A Comparative Study of Pseudotyped Vectors and Transduction Enhancers.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered natural killer (CAR-NK) cell therapy has demonstrated favorable safety profiles and considerable potential for "off-the-shelf" applications in cancer immunotherapy. However, because NK cells possess intrinsic antiviral properties, lentiviral vector (LV)-mediated gene delivery into NK cells remains substantially less efficient than in T cells, motivating efforts to optimize transduction conditions. In this study, we performed a preliminary, systematic comparison of the transduction efficiencies of three pseudotyped LVs-vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein (VSV-G), baboon endogenous retrovirus (BaEV), and feline endogenous retrovirus (RD114) envelope glycoprotein-in NK92 cells under various infection durations and multiplicity of infection (MOI) conditions. We further evaluated the differential effects of five transduction enhancers (TEs)-polybrene, dextran, protamine sulfate (PS), PAP248-286, and poloxamer F108-on the transduction efficiency of these three pseudotyped LVs. At 24h, BaEV-LV showed the highest mean transduction efficiency among the three pseudotyped LVs in NK92 cells, whereas RD114-LV showed the lowest. Polybrene enhanced BaEV-LV transduction by approximately 3.6-fold at 1μg/mL (from 10.40% to 37.07%), with comparable enhancement observed across the tested range of 1-10μg/mL. PAP248-286 increased RD114-LV transduction from 0.35% to 16.73% at 100μg/mL, the highest concentration tested. These results provide a preliminary experimental basis for optimizing lentiviral transduction conditions in NK92 cells; further validation using CAR constructs and primary NK cells will be required to assess the applicability of these findings to CAR-NK cell generation.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Moderate HBV DNA Levels Are Associated With the Highest Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B.
items.abstract: Although serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels are generally considered to correlate linearly with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in chronic hepatitis B, recent evidence suggests a non-linear relationship, with peak risk at moderate levels. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively assess HCC risk across HBV DNA levels. The systematic review and meta-analysis were reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched through August 2025. HBV DNA levels were categorized as low ( 10  IU/mL), moderate (3.3-7 log 10  IU/mL), or high (> 7 log 10  IU/mL). The primary outcome was HCC incidence. Hazard ratios (HRs) were synthesized using the generic inverse-variance method. A total of 45 studies including 129,950 patients were analysed. Pooled HCC incidence rates per 100 person-years were 0.304 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.248-0.361), 0.859 (95% CI 0.751-0.966), and 0.409 (95% CI 0.307-0.511) in the low, moderate, and high HBV DNA groups, respectively. Sensitivity analyses applying a stricter upper HBV DNA threshold and more restrictive classification criteria showed a similar pattern, with the highest pooled incidence in the moderate group. Subgroup analyses by treatment status, HBeAg status, alanine aminotransferase levels, and presence of cirrhosis generally supported the overall pattern. The moderate group carried a higher risk than both the low (pooled HR 2.95, 95% CI 2.41-3.61) and high groups (pooled HR 3.56, 95% CI 2.69-4.72). Meta-regression further demonstrated a higher HCC incidence rate in the moderate versus high HBV DNA group (β = 0.350 per 100 person-years, 95% CI 0.191-0.509; p < 0.001). Moderate HBV DNA levels were associated with the highest pooled HCC incidence across the predefined categories.

items.title: High-frequency spleen stiffness measurement for noninvasive detection of esophageal varices and high-risk varices: A pilot study.
items.abstract: While esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) remains the reference standard for detecting esophageal varices (EV) and high-risk varices (HRV), it is invasive and frequently unnecessary in low-risk patients with cirrhosis. This pilot study compared the diagnostic performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM) with that of liver stiffness measurement (LSM), the aspartate transaminase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI), and the FIB-4 score for predicting EV and HRV. Patients with cirrhosis were prospectively recruited. Participants underwent SSM, LSM, and EGD, alongside calculation of APRI and FIB-4 scores. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed, and areas under the curves (AUCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and maximal Youden indices were compared. EV and HRV were present in 18 (47.4%) and 6 (15.8%) of 38 eligible patients, respectively. SSM was significantly higher in patients with EV and HRV than those without, while LSM did not differ. SSM demonstrated the highest AUCs for EV (0.906, 95% CI: 0.767-0.992; p < 0.001) and HRV (0.891, 95% CI: 0.772-0.985; p < 0.001) detection. SSM significantly outperformed LSM for both EV (ΔAUC: 0.235; p = 0.003) and HRV (ΔAUC: 0.279; p = 0.012). Using optimal cut-offs of 39.2 kPa and 47.5 kPa, SSM yielded 88.9% sensitivity and 85.0% specificity for EV, and 100% sensitivity and 75.0% specificity for HRV. High-frequency SSM demonstrated superior performance compared with conventional LSM for identifying EV and HRV in patients with cirrhosis. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate standardized cut-offs.

items.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as a key driver of clinically significant fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), which is linked to more advanced liver disease. We aimed to assess the relationship between T2DM and fibrosis severity in patients with MASLD. We analyzed 92 patients with MASLD, excluding those with chronic viral hepatitis or significant alcohol intake. Anthropometric, laboratory, and ultrasound data were collected. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) and steatosis were assessed by transient elastography. Associations between T2DM and clinically significant fibrosis (LSM ≥8kPa) were evaluated using correlation and multivariable logistic regression. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was present in 55.4% of patients. Patients with T2DM had a higher prevalence of LSM ≥8kPa than non-diabetic individuals (39.2% vs 4.9%; p<.0001), corresponding to a 28-fold higher odds of clinically significant fibrosis. A moderate correlation was observed between T2DM and fibrosis stage (ρ=0.451; p<.001). After adjustment for age, body mass index, triglycerides, and sex, T2DM remained independently associated with clinically significant fibrosis, conferring a 36-fold higher odds (OR, 36.13; 95% CI, 3.08-423.0; p=0.004). Type 2 diabetes mellitus is strongly associated with clinically significant liver fibrosis in MASLD. These findings support integrated hepatometabolic risk stratification and targeted fibrosis screening in patients with T2DM.

items.title: Specific infectious risks in the urological operating room: Epidemiology and prevention of exposure to blood and body fluids and human papillomavirus.
items.abstract: Urological surgery exposes practitioners to occupational infectious risks specific to the operating theatre. This article focuses specifically on blood exposure accidents (BEA) involving bloodborne viruses (HBV, HCV, HIV) and exposure to aerosols potentially containing human papillomavirus (HPV) during the treatment of HPV-induced lesions. A narrative (non-systematic) literature review was conducted on the risk of occupational exposure to HPV and blood exposure accidents, prioritizing literature reviews in order to synthesize available data and recommendations, supplemented, where relevant, by original studies providing additional data. This article synthesizes the available epidemiological data and institutional recommendations (HAS 2023-2024, 2019 interministerial instruction, 2011 HCSP report, CNOM 2025) and proposes a prevention strategy along with an algorithm for post-exposure management, presented according to two practice settings: salaried hospital-based surgeon and self-employed (private practice) surgeon. BEAs represent the predominant risk (5.7 per 100 surgeons/year), with theoretical percutaneous transmission rates of 30% for HBV (HBeAg+), 1.8% for HCV, and 0.32% for HIV. In urology, open surgery (cystectomy, prostatectomy) carries a high risk, whereas endoscopic, laparoscopy and robot-assisted surgery are associated with a lower risk. Occupational exposure to HPV via smoke plumes during the treatment of condylomas is documented (genotypes 6 and 11), but its occupational risk remains poorly quantified. The main difference between salaried and self-employed practice lies in the organization of post-exposure care: the self-employed surgeon reports the incident to the CPAM (French National Health Insurance Fund) and accesses post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) through emergency departments or CeGIDD centers, whereas this pathway is coordinated by the occupational health department or the affiliated emergency department for salaried physicians. As this constitutes a workplace accident or occupational disease, there is also a fundamental difference in healthcare cost coverage between these two practice settings. The therapeutic window for PEP (ideally<4hours) requires that every practitioner identify their care pathway before any blood exposure accident occurs. Standard precautions, HBV vaccination, and viral load reduction through antiretroviral therapy considerably limit residual risk.

items.title: Nutritional care and short-term mortality in alcohol-associated hepatitis: a real-world two-center study.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high mortality. Malnutrition is highly prevalent, and nutrition represents a central therapeutic target alongside corticosteroids and alcohol abstinence, yet real-world implementation remains unclear. We aimed to assess adherence to nutritional guidelines and its association with mortality. In this retrospective cohort study, we included 157 patients hospitalized with AH at a tertiary and a secondary center (2019-2023). Data on nutritional management and mortality were extracted from medical records. Cut off for energy intake was categorized at 21.4 kcal/kg/day, based on the cohort median, in patients with ≥66% of inpatient days documented. Differences in guideline adherence between centers were analyzed using χ 2 and Wilcoxon tests. Survival was assessed with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank test. Most individuals had severe AH (66%) and 72% had liver cirrhosis. Median age was 57 years, 36% were female. Malnutrition risk screening was performed in 85% of patients, with 39% classified as at risk. Dietitian involvement was higher at the tertiary center (83% vs 42%), associated with more specialized nutritional care. Energy intake was more frequently monitored at the tertiary center (87% vs 48%). Parenteral nutrition was used more often than enteral nutrition (28% vs 11%), particularly at the tertiary center. Low energy intake was associated with higher 28-day mortality (p=0.02). Real-world nutritional care in AH is inconsistent and often deviates from established guidelines. Our findings suggest that achieving adequate energy intake may improve survival. These results highlight the need for flexible, patient-centered nutritional strategies, particularly in settings with limited hepatology expertise.

items.title: International expert perspectives on three-dimensional virtual hepatectomy: clinical value, selective use, and implementation barriers.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) liver reconstruction supports patient-specific anatomical understanding and operative planning. However, how experts integrate 3D imaging across different types of hepatectomy, combine it with indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence, and overcome barriers to broader implementation remain incompletely characterized. A non-anonymous, web-based survey was conducted in 2023 among 20 international HPB experts. Perceived utility, procedure-specific reconstruction and volumetry, use with ICG fluorescence, model-generation workflows, and implementation barriers were summarized descriptively. Eighty-two percent rated 3D reconstruction highly useful for avoiding intraoperative misorientation and 71% for obtaining an adequate surgical margin. Perceived utility was highest for complex anatomical resections and lowest for left lateral sectionectomy. Portal vein, hepatic vein, and tumor reconstruction were routinely used, whereas hepatic artery and bile duct reconstruction were selectively added. Combined use of 3D imaging and ICG fluorescence was preferred by 74-79% for anterior/posterior sectionectomy, segment 7/8 resection, and hemihepatectomy. Surgeons were involved in model generation in 59% of institutions; cost and technical difficulty were the leading barriers to dissemination. Experts valued 3D virtual hepatectomy primarily for maintaining intraoperative orientation and guiding an appropriate transection plane with an adequate surgical margin. Selective, question-driven use and reduced reconstruction burden may support broader implementation.

items.title: Carboplatin tissue pharmacokinetics following intraperitoneal and systemic treatment: a microdialysis porcine study.
items.abstract: Understanding carboplatin's tissue pharmacokinetics is critical for assessing its locoregional potential in Hyperthermic and Normothermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC, NIPEC) in ovarian cancer. This study assessed carboplatin exposure in tissues associated with ovarian cancer carcinomatosis across clinically relevant treatment regimens, using microdialysis in a healthy porcine model. Animals were divided into three groups receiving HIPEC, NIPEC, or intravenous (IV) carboplatin. A minor cytoreductive surgery was performed in the HIPEC and NIPEC groups, followed by carboplatin perfusion (800 mg/m 2 ). The IV group received a 30 min carboplatin infusion (625 mg). Unbound carboplatin concentrations were measured by microdialysis at intra-abdominal target sites during and after chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was parietal peritoneum AUC 0-∞ between groups. Parietal peritoneal AUC 0-∞ was higher after HIPEC than after IV treatment (geometric mean ratio 2.37; 95% CI 1.08-5.17), whereas the NIPEC-IV (1.61; 0.73-3.53) and the exploratory HIPEC-NIPEC (1.47; 0.58-3.73) comparisons were inconclusive. Omental exposure showed a similar numerical pattern. IV treatment showed numerically higher exposure in plasma, rectum, liver, and superficial stomach. Perfusate carboplatin concentration decreased by approximately 32%. Greater inter-individual variability was evident following intraperitoneal chemotherapy. The intraperitoneal regimens achieved numerically higher carboplatin exposure in the peritoneal lining than the IV regimen, with lower systemic exposure but greater variability. The study was not powered to determine whether hyperthermia affects carboplatin pharmacokinetics. These findings may inform further development and clinical evaluation of intraperitoneal carboplatin chemotherapy in ovarian cancer.

items.title: Human Pregnane X Receptor Modulates Sex-Dependent Hepatic Oxidative Stress and Inflammatory Responses in Alcohol-Induced Liver Injury.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) remains a major global health burden with limited targeted therapies. Although the pregnane X receptor (PXR) has been implicated in ALD pathogenesis, the specific contribution of human PXR signaling to ethanol-induced liver injury remains unclear. Here, we investigated the impact of human PXR on ethanol-induced hepatotoxicity, histopathology, inflammation, oxidative stress, immune-cell composition, and hepatic transcriptional profiles. Male and female wild-type (WT, C57BL/6N) and PXR-humanized (hPXR) mice were subjected to the chronic-plus-binge ethanol regimen, followed by comprehensive hepatic and systemic profiling. Ethanol-fed female hPXR mice developed more severe steatosis and hepatotoxicity than their WT counterparts. This exacerbated liver injury was accompanied by elevated circulating acetaldehyde, increased hepatic hydrogen peroxide levels, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, enhanced NF-κB activation, and reduced mitochondrial ALDH2 protein expression and activity, consistent with impaired acetaldehyde detoxification and ROS accumulation. Hepatic transcriptomics identified differential expression of genes associated with xenobiotic metabolism and pathways potentially involved in non-oxidative ethanol metabolism, including members of the Ces2a and Sult2a gene families. Splenic and mesenteric lymph node CD3+ T-cell frequencies and circulating IL-5 concentrations were elevated in females regardless of genotype or ethanol exposure, indicating baseline sex-dependent immune differences rather than broad human PXR-dependent systemic immune activation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that human PXR promotes susceptibility to ethanol-induced liver injury, particularly in females via impaired acetaldehyde clearance, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and altered hepatic gene expression as potential mechanisms. These results establish hPXR mice as a translational model for dissecting human PXR-dependent mechanisms and therapeutic targets in ALD.
